rows.reason: The typed body requires the actual checked DWORD-vector header and owning intrusive stock-list sentinel/nodes. Impl keeps preload_census and stock_queue as independent std::vectors, and this site only logs. There is no borrowed native list to clear; introducing its allocation/ownership lifecycle exceeds a small view adapter. No fabricated empty containers were passed.

The body computes the native registry +10h max-cell-height over its first layer. NavStream owns parsed TerrainGridLayerRecords; GameAvoidZoneRegistry keeps a vector and no authoritative max_cell_height field or consumer. A temporary native registry would discard the only body result.

OFF already calls read_browser_groups_after_keyword, the same body that read_browser_groups_block delegates to after expecting the keyword. The scene reader has consumed that keyword. Calling the whole entry would duplicate existing logic or only replay a constant keyword.

OFF already calls read_traffic_block_after_keyword, which executes read_traffic_block_body and the same clear callback as read_traffic_block. The keyword is already consumed. Adding the whole entry duplicates the OFF parser or requires replaying a constant keyword.

The body allocates and links native command records at database+14Ch, while this host stores command/target on GameSceneEntityRecord for direct issuance. Its deferred-reference resolver deliberately walks a different empty SceneCommandQueue. A native append would be unconsumed; copying strings back from a throwaway record would only round-trip existing values.

The body deletes pending objects in native database+28h..+2Ch. Host-created named entities are owned separately in Impl::named_entity_images; no producer populates this native pending vector. Calling it would process only an empty constructor-initialized range and would not destroy actual host pending objects.

The native body looks up a name-hash node at owner+4 and returns node+8; this stand-in copies a parsed ScenePropertyBlock. There is no native name-intern table/key on this publication site. Publishing the same block through an invented callback would not execute the lookup contract.

The native command list has no host producer: 00469610 is recorded as strings on entity records and the resolver uses a separate empty queue. Calling the destructive native list walk would receive only empty state rather than clearing the host's live command records.

Readiness marks this nodef: the source entry is a singleton descriptor-table row, not a directly callable definition. GameAvoidZoneRegistry is a separate typed singleton with vector-owned layers, not the native 14h object plus singleton lifetime-manager composition. Returning the existing typed singleton through a callback would only round-trip it.

Readiness selects scene_entity_class_table as a nodef row. The host already iterates that table and calls scene_class_map_register_004ee250 into the live native class map under kSceneDatabaseCc15Bound=true; the mission-frame caller already invokes this registration. Another call would duplicate OFF work, not replace it.

Readiness's selected source entry is nodef. The whole native tokenizer constructor requires an image-shaped 838h tokenizer, canonical NativeString process, and native VFS stream ownership. This host caches file text and parses through SceneLexer; it keeps none of that actual tokenizer graph. A temporary constructor would leave the live lexer unchanged.

The whole body needs an actual 38h property record with a uniquely owned current-CRT string or a genuine enum declaration at +28h, plus canonical GameNativeStringProcess. weather_bag contains parsed SceneProperty values and this stand-in only records writes; no genuine raw property/enum ownership graph exists. A scratch property would discard its result or round-trip the input token.

record_remap_texture_name always returns an empty string and the host owns neither render-resources+66Ch nor the texture-manager/reference-counted texture graph. Calling the setter would require constant names and invented resource storage rather than real scene remap state.

The body only calls a supplied VFS vtable+4 opener and stores its returned pointer in the output slot. A vtable shim over owner_.read_vfs_file would do all existing host work before handing that same host result back; no native VFS provider/name/stream image is retained here. This would be a callback round trip.
